title: morphological study of Balinese culinary terms and their equivalents in Balinese sentences
abstract: Many terms related to Balinese cuisine need to be documented to prevent them from falling into disuse or disappearing. Beyond describing linguistic aspects from a morphological perspective, this study also aims to document Balinese culinary terms that remain active and evolving within the Balinese community through their usage in Balinese sentences. Balinese culinary terms are highly diverse and numerous. These terms can be analyzed morphologically—covering base forms, as well as forms with prefixes, infixes, suffixes, and confixes—and examined in terms of their usage within the context of communication in Balinese sentences.

title: Understanding the Pre-partnership Stage in Subnational International Cooperation
journal: RSF Conference Series: Business, Management and Social Sciences
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed destination marketing by enabling the creation of visually compelling promotional content. While AI-generated visuals offer new opportunities for tourism promotion, concerns about their perceived authenticity and fairness may influence tourists’ behavioral intentions. This study examines how the perceived authenticity of AI-generated visuals and perceived justice affect tourist patronage intention toward Bali as a tourism destination. A quantitative explanatory research design was employed, using a cross-sectional survey of 130 valid respondents who had viewed AI-generated tourism visuals of Bali. Data were collected via an online questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results show that perceived authenticity of AI-generated visuals has a positive and significant effect on tourist patronage intention (β = 0.299, p = 0.002). Perceived justice also has a positive and significant effect on tourist patronage intention and demonstrates a stronger effect (β = 0.611, p < 0.001). The findings indicate that tourists’ patronage intentions are shaped by both the perceived authenticity of AI-generated destination visuals and perceptions of fairness in destination management. The study contributes to the emerging literature on AI-enabled tourism marketing by integrating visual authenticity and perceived justice into a single framework and provides practical implications for destination marketing organizations to use AI-generated visual content while maintaining credible communication and responsible destination management.

The use of drones in public safety: mapping applications, potential and limitations
abstract: Purpose This study aims to analyse the scientific production on the use of drones in public safety, identifying patterns of development, collaboration networks, intellectual structure, thematic evolution and research gaps in the field. Design/methodology/approach The research adopts a quantitative, descriptive and exploratory approach based on bibliometric analysis. Data were collected from the Scopus database, covering the period from 2021 to 2025. A total of 361 journal articles were analysed using performance indicators and science mapping techniques. The study employs PyBibX for performance analysis and VOSviewer and Bibliometrix (R) for co-authorship, co-citation, keyword co-occurrence and conceptual structure analysis through Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA). Additionally, a PRISMA-based protocol was applied to identify a core set of 65 articles for thematic classification. Findings The results indicate that research on drones in public safety is a rapidly expanding and highly collaborative field, characterised by strong internationalisation and interdisciplinary integration. The intellectual structure is supported by multiple interconnected domains, including artificial intelligence, signal processing, autonomous systems, and security studies. Thematic analysis reveals that drones function as central elements in the transition towards data-driven policing, enabling real-time monitoring, predictive analytics and operational optimisation. However, the study also identifies significant challenges related to regulatory gaps, cybersecurity risks, institutional barriers and ethical concerns, particularly regarding privacy, legitimacy and social acceptance. Research limitations/implications The study is limited to the Scopus database, English-language journal articles, and the 2021–2025 period, which may exclude relevant contributions from other sources or earlier foundational studies. Future research should incorporate multiple databases, extend temporal coverage, and explore qualitative and empirical approaches, particularly regarding governance, regulation, and societal impacts. Practical implications The findings provide insights for policymakers, public safety agencies, and practitioners by highlighting key applications, technological requirements, and implementation challenges associated with drone adoption. The study supports strategic decision-making related to resource allocation, operational integration, and technological investment in security systems. Social implications The increasing use of drones in public safety has significant implications for the relationship between the state and society, particularly in terms of surveillance, privacy, and institutional trust. The results emphasize the need for transparent governance, procedural justice, and proportional use of technology to ensure social legitimacy and public acceptance. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature by providing a comprehensive bibliometric and conceptual mapping of drones in public safety, integrating technological, organizational, and sociotechnical perspectives. It advances the field by proposing an analytical interpretation of UAVs as platforms of datafication, supporting the transition towards data-driven security systems.

title: The Diffusion of Cohabitation Among Immigrants in Europe: The Role of the National Cohabitation Context
abstract: Abstract Immigrants and their descendants constitute an increasing share of European populations, yet research on how immigrant background shapes the cohabitation experience remains limited. This study investigates how generational status at the individual level and national context at the macro level influence the likelihood of ever having cohabited. Our central proposition is that the diffusion of cohabitation among immigrants is more pronounced in countries where the practice is common and socially accepted among the native population. We analysed pooled data from the European Social Survey (ESS; 2002–2023), encompassing 444,794 respondents across 32 countries. Mixed-effects modelling points to generational adaptation: descendants of immigrants are more likely to have ever cohabited than immigrants, though the magnitude of this difference varies across countries. The prevalence of cohabitation among natives emerges as a strong contextual predictor, increasing the likelihood of cohabitation for both immigrants and their descendants, and narrowing migrant-native differences in settings where cohabitation is more common. This study contributes to the literature by demonstrating that lifetime cohabitation among immigrants and their descendants is not merely a product of individual traits but is fundamentally shaped by the normative climate of the host country.

title: The Influence of Live Streaming Promotion and Online Customer Review on Consumer Fashion Purchase Intention on Lazada in Depok City
journal: Lead Journal of Economy and Administration
abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of live streaming promotions and online customer reviews on consumer purchase intention for fashion products on the Lazada e-commerce platform in Depok City, both partially and simultaneously. A quantitative approach was employed, utilizing a questionnaire as the research instrument. The sample consisted of 120 respondents selected via non-probability sampling using a purposive sampling technique. Data analysis was conducted using SPSS software (version 26), encompassing validity tests, reliability tests, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression analysis, the coefficient of determination (R²), and hypothesis testing via t-tests (partial) and F-tests (simultaneous). The results indicate that live streaming promotions have a significant negative effect on purchase intention, whereas online customer reviews have a significant positive effect. Simultaneously, both live streaming promotions and online customer reviews significantly influence consumer purchase intention for fashion products on Lazada in Depok City. The coefficient of determination reveals that the two independent variables explain 39.9% of the variation in purchase intention, while the remaining 60.1% is attributed to variables not included in this study. These findings suggest that enhancing the quality of customer reviews and optimizing live streaming promotional strategies can be effective measures for boosting consumer purchase intention on e-commerce platforms.

Tree Structure and Turnover in a Peruvian Premontane Amazon Forest
journal: Jurnal Manajemen Hutan Tropika (Journal of Tropical Forest Management)
abstract: Humid tropical forests are increasingly exposed to fire, yet local diversity, stand structure, and species composition may respond differently. We compared tree communities in lower and upper sectors of a university reserve near Tingo María, Peru, using 27 rectangular 500 m² sampling units (13 lower, 14 upper). The upper sector showed field evidence of fire, although fire history was confounded with elevation and no pre-fire inventory was available. We assessed alpha and beta diversity, diameter and height structure, and species and family importance values at the sampling-unit level. Species composition differed robustly between sectors for presence-absence and abundance data (PERMANOVA, p-value < 0.001), whereas multivariate dispersion did not. After false-discovery-rate correction, alpha-diversity and structural variables showed no confirmed differences. Nevertheless, medium-to-large effect sizes indicated trends toward lower mean height and emergent-tree representation, and larger crown diameter and understory representation, in the upper sector; these trends were not confirmed at this sample size. Dominance shifted: upper-sector importance was density-driven for Senefeldera inclinata, whereas lower-sector importance was basal-area-driven for Cedrelinga cateniformis. The data therefore demonstrate taxonomic turnover but cannot attribute sector differences specifically to fire rather than elevation-associated conditions. Repeated integrated monitoring is needed to distinguish these effects.
